verses.text: The angel of the LORD went up from Gilgal to Bokim and said, "I brought you up out of Egypt and led you into the land I promised your ancestors. I said, 'I will never break my covenant with you,
and you must not make any treaty with the people of this land. You must tear down their altars.' But you have not obeyed me. Why have you done this?
So now I tell you: I will not drive them out ahead of you. They will be like thorns in your sides, and their gods will be a trap for you."
When the angel of the LORD said these things to all the Israelites, the people cried loudly.
They called that place Bokim, which means Crying, and they offered sacrifices there to the LORD.
After Joshua had sent the people away, each of the Israelites went to take the land given to them.
The people served the LORD all the time Joshua was alive, and all the time of the elders who lived after him and had seen all the great things the LORD had done for Israel.
Joshua son of Nun, the servant of the LORD, died at the age of a hundred and ten.
They buried him on his own land at Timnath Heres in the hill country of Ephraim, north of Mount Gaash.
After that whole generation had died, another generation grew up who did not know the LORD or what he had done for Israel.
Then the Israelites did what was evil in the LORD's eyes and served the Baals.
They left the LORD, the God of their ancestors, who had brought them out of Egypt. They followed and worshipped the gods of the peoples around them, and they made the LORD angry.
They left the LORD and served Baal and the Ashtoreths.
In his anger against Israel, the LORD handed them over to raiders who robbed them. He sold them to their enemies all around, and they could no longer stand against them.
Whenever Israel went out to fight, the LORD's hand was against them to defeat them, just as he had warned and sworn to them. They were in great trouble.
Then the LORD raised up judges, leaders who saved them from the raiders.

Yet they did not listen to their judges. They were unfaithful to the LORD and worshipped other gods and bowed down to them. They quickly turned away from the path their ancestors had walked, the path of obeying the LORD's commands. They did not do as their ancestors had done.

Whenever the LORD raised up a judge for them, he was with that judge and saved them from their enemies as long as the judge lived. The LORD felt sorry for them as they groaned under those who treated them cruelly and crushed them.

But when the judge died, the people went back to even worse ways than their ancestors. They followed other gods, serving and worshipping them. They refused to give up their evil practices and stubborn ways.
So the LORD was very angry with Israel. He said, "This nation has broken the covenant I gave their ancestors and has not listened to me.
So I will no longer drive out ahead of them any of the nations Joshua left when he died.
I will use them to test Israel and see whether they will keep the way of the LORD and walk in it as their ancestors did."
So the LORD let those nations stay. He did not drive them out quickly or give them into Joshua's hands.
